label: mid-sequence o/a/f-type input after h/j/0/1/z context (original phase)
explanation: Fires almost only during the original input phase (91% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (9%); essentially never during copy. Peaks at t=3-6 and never fires at t=0-1. Favors first occurrences of a token (93% of mass). The strongest input tokens are o (7.9x lift, 31% of mass), then a, f, p, u, g. It is also boosted when earlier inputs include h, j, 0, 1 or z (first_tok h or 1 gives about 4x lift; prev2_tok j/0/1/h gives about 4x), and by having more digits in the sequence. The top activations are o or a at positions 3-5 after prefixes like h h 0 y f or 1 0 j. The best simple predicate (o/a/f/p/u/g input in the original phase, with at least 2 earlier h/j/0/1/z inputs) only gets dev F1 0.32 and mass recall 0.43. Broader versions reach 0.72-0.86 mass recall but under 10% precision. Many activations fall outside any token rule (e.g. c, l, 0 or <DEL> after h/j/0 prefixes), so this looks like a distributed readout of input token plus history, not one clean concept.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+3.80), orig0=1 (+3.60), orig0=z (+3.26), orig1=h (+2.95), phase=0 & in_tok=a (+2.83), orig0=l (+2.78). Lower it: phase=2 (-6.50), in_tok=h (-4.58), in_tok=1 (-4.53), prev2_tok=- (-4.47).
